title: The complete radius-2 atlas of the pinwheel law
claim: The 1-collared tiles of all pinwheel patches (a tile with every tile touching it, in the tile's own affine frame, with handedness) form a set of 193 keys closed under Conway's cut, generated from one triangle; 108 are complete, in 54 mirror pairs. Cutting a complete collar four times leaves every dart whose tail lies in the central tile's descendants farther than 3 from the edge, so the radius-2 atlas of every pinwheel tiling is computed exactly from the complete collars. It has 1,168 rooted codes, each with exactly one oriented label (PINWHEEL-NATIVE-20261107-001B's), so in every pinwheel tiling each edge's label is a function of the unlabelled planar map within radius 2; at radius 1 there are 198 codes, 9 with two labels. The atlas equals the interior codes of the geometric level-7 patch.
failure_conditions: The collar search does not close, or a collar's image under the cut is missing from the closed set.
A dart whose tail lies in a complete collar's descendants is within distance 3 of the edge of the cut collar at the declared j.
Two different oriented labels share one radius-2 code in the atlas.
The atlas differs from the radius-2 codes of the geometric level-7 patch.
foundation_claim_scope: Every pinwheel tiling (every finite patch congruent to part of a level-k patch of one triangle); radius-2 codes of the planar map; exact closure and finite computation.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: arguments by hand (touching children have touching parents; legal patches placed inside interior tiles of T_2 of both handednesses); check.py (about 7 minutes) verifies the closure at 193 keys, 108 complete keys in mirror pairs, the edge test at four cuts, 1,168 conflict-free radius-2 codes and 198 radius-1 codes with 9 conflicts, and equality with the independently computed level-7 patch at both radii; controls (two cuts, a search stopped at level 3, shuffled labels) all fail as required; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known method: collared tiles closed under substitution (Anderson-Putnam; for the pinwheel, Barge-Diamond-Hunton-Sadun 2010 and Frettloh-Whitehead-Whittaker 2014); the combinatorial pinwheel rule is Kenyon-Stephenson's (2019). The radius-2 atlas and its readability theorem are new as far as found.
